name: NY-26
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+11 district with incumbent Tim Kennedy running for re-election
Kennedy has raised $2.3M and holds $1.2M on hand; Dennis Hannon shows no reported fundraising

model.rationale: The district's D+11 lean, Kennedy's incumbency, his large financial advantage over a challenger with no reported fundraising, and market pricing near 97% all point in the same direction, with no evidence of a competitive race.
model.watch: Any polling or rating that shows Hannon gaining traction, or a sharply Republican national environment in New York, would be the signal to reassess.

overview:
Western New York's 26th District leans about eleven points Democratic, and first-term Representative Tim Kennedy is running for re-election. Kennedy has raised $2.3 million and holds $1.2 million on hand, while Republican Dennis Hannon shows no reported fundraising. Prediction markets price the Democratic side at roughly 97%, and no major race ratings list the contest as competitive.

No public general-election polls are available, so expectations rest on district fundamentals, incumbency, and money. The combination of a favorable lean, a well-funded incumbent, and a lightly financed challenger makes this a Safe Democratic race, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of polling rather than any specific signal of a closer contest. A significant shift in the national environment or unexpected challenger resources would be needed to change the picture.
